name: Magur
description: A star 149 parsecs away, 39 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90037: radius 39.341 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 371.904 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.089) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90037: effective temperature 4044 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.041)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90037: distance 148.588 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.064), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 149 parsecs away, 39 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 372 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,044 K, so 39.341 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 90037: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 168592
quotes.card: HD 168592, also designated HR 6862 and named Magur, is a solitary star located in the southern constellation Corona Australis.
quotes.introduction: It is faintly visible to the naked eye as an orange-hued star with an apparent magnitude of 5.07.
